The invention relates to a system for treating molecules or particles of interest that are transported in a viscoelastic liquid. More specifically, the system is designed to concentrate, stack, and/or purify such molecules or particles while they are carried by the liquid through a dedicated treatment device.

During a concentration phase, the system establishes a laminar flow of the viscoelastic liquid through the device. The device comprises a concentration area through which the liquid passes. This concentration area has an intake cross-section that is larger than the cross-section of each outlet channel connected to it. This difference in cross-section contributes to the controlled movement and positioning of the molecules or particles within the device.

An electric field is applied between the intake and the outlet of the concentration area. The electric field is oriented so as to oppose the direction of flow of the viscoelastic liquid. As a result, the molecules or particles of interest are retained within the concentration area or in the vicinity of that area, allowing them to accumulate, become concentrated, stacked, and/or separated from other components present in the liquid.

After the concentration phase, the system uses a modulation means to control the applied electric field. Rather than completely eliminating the electric field, the modulation means applies a nonzero electric field having an intensity lower than the intensity used during the concentration phase. This reduced field may help maintain partial retention, prevent uncontrolled dispersion of the molecules or particles, and allow a more controlled release, transfer, or subsequent treatment of the concentrated species.

In this way, the system combines laminar flow in a viscoelastic liquid, a concentration geometry with a larger intake cross-section than outlet channel cross-sections, and controlled electric-field modulation to efficiently treat molecules or particles of interest.
outputs.L4:
A system is provided for concentrating, stacking, purifying, separating, or otherwise treating molecules, particles, cells, beads, analytes, or other suspended species that are carried within a viscoelastic liquid. The system includes a fluidic device, such as a channel, conduit, capillary, microfluidic chip, or other flow path, through which the viscoelastic liquid is caused to flow under laminar-flow conditions. The viscoelastic liquid may contain polymers, surfactants, biological materials, or other additives that impart elastic behavior to the fluid while maintaining a controlled and predictable flow profile.

During operation, a sample containing the molecules or particles of interest is introduced into the device and transported through the flow path by pressure-driven flow, electrokinetic flow, or another suitable pumping mechanism. A concentration region is established within the device, for example at a selected portion of the channel or near an electrode-defined zone. In this concentration region, an electric field is applied in a direction that opposes the movement of the molecules or particles carried by the laminar flow. The opposing electric field is selected so that electrophoretic, dielectrophoretic, electroosmotic, or other electrically induced forces counteract the hydrodynamic transport of the species. As a result, the molecules or particles are slowed, immobilized, retained, stacked, or accumulated within the concentration region rather than being swept downstream with the bulk liquid.

The magnitude of the electric field during this concentration phase may be adjusted according to the size, charge, mobility, polarizability, or other physical or chemical properties of the species being processed. In some implementations, the field strength is sufficient to balance the drag force exerted by the flowing viscoelastic liquid, thereby forming a localized concentrated band or plug of material. In other implementations, the field strength may be selected to concentrate only a subset of species while allowing other components, contaminants, carrier fluid, or background matrix materials to pass through the device. In this manner, the system may be used not only for concentration but also for purification, enrichment, fractionation, washing, buffer exchange, or selective retention.

After a desired amount of molecules or particles has been retained in the concentration region, the system transitions to a post-concentration phase. Rather than simply turning off the electric field, the system applies a weaker but nonzero electric field. This reduced electric field is lower than the field used during the concentration phase but remains sufficient to influence the retained species. By maintaining a controlled residual electrical force, the system allows the concentrated material to be handled in a more precise and stable manner. For example, the weaker field may prevent sudden release, dispersion, diffusion-driven spreading, or uncontrolled downstream transport of the concentrated species. It may also allow the retained material to be gradually eluted, repositioned, further purified, mixed with reagents, transferred to another region of the device, or prepared for detection, analysis, reaction, collection, or downstream processing.

The use of a nonzero electric field after concentration can therefore provide improved control over the concentrated sample. The retained molecules or particles may be released at a controlled rate, held in place while the surrounding liquid is exchanged, or subjected to additional treatment steps without losing the benefits of the concentration process. In certain embodiments, the reduced field may be dynamically varied over time, applied in pulses, combined with changes in flow rate, or coordinated with additional electric fields or pressure gradients to achieve a desired manipulation protocol.

The system may include one or more electrodes positioned to generate the opposing electric field in the concentration region, a power supply or voltage controller configured to apply both the concentration field and the weaker post-concentration field, and a flow controller configured to establish and maintain laminar flow of the viscoelastic liquid. Sensors, detectors, feedback controls, reservoirs, valves, or collection chambers may also be included. The system can be implemented in analytical, preparative, diagnostic, biomedical, chemical, environmental, or industrial applications where small amounts of target species must be enriched or processed from a flowing viscoelastic medium.

In summary, the system operates by flowing a viscoelastic liquid containing target molecules or particles through a device under laminar conditions, applying an electric field that opposes the flow to retain and concentrate the target species in a defined concentration area, and then reducing the electric field to a weaker nonzero value to permit controlled handling of the concentrated material after the concentration step.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called the definite article, and it is used when we talk about something specific or already known. For example, when someone says “the book,” they usually mean a particular book, not just any book.

Although “the” may seem simple, it helps make sentences clear. It tells the listener or reader that the speaker is referring to a certain person, place, thing, or idea. We say “the sun” because there is only one sun in our sky, and we say “the teacher” when both people in the conversation know which teacher is being discussed.

The word “the” also gives language structure and precision. Without it, many sentences would sound incomplete or confusing. For example, “I went to store” sounds unnatural, while “I went to the store” clearly explains where the person went.

In short, “the” may be a tiny word, but it has a big purpose. It helps us identify specific things, make our meaning clear, and speak more naturally in English. Sometimes, the smallest words are the most important.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style description of an invention for concentrating molecules or particles in a viscoelastic liquid using laminar flow and an opposing electric field, including numbered system components.
counterfactuals.output:
## Patent-Style Description

### Title  
**Systems and Methods for Concentrating Molecules or Particles in a Viscoelastic Liquid Using Laminar Flow and an Opposing Electric Field**

### Technical Field  
The present disclosure relates generally to microfluidic and fluid-processing systems, and more particularly to systems and methods for concentrating charged molecules, biomolecules, colloids, cells, nanoparticles, microparticles, or other suspended species in a viscoelastic liquid by combining laminar fluid flow with an opposing electric field.

### Background  
Concentration, focusing, trapping, or enrichment of molecules and particles is important in chemical analysis, biological assays, diagnostics, sample preparation, and materials processing. Conventional concentration techniques may require membranes, filters, centrifugation, evaporation, or complex microfabricated structures. These approaches can introduce clogging, sample loss, thermal damage, or limited compatibility with fragile biological materials.

Microfluidic systems provide precise control over small volumes of liquid and can maintain laminar flow due to low Reynolds-number operating conditions. Electric fields may be used to drive electrophoretic or electroosmotic transport of charged species. However, in Newtonian liquids, the balance between pressure-driven flow and electric-field-driven motion may provide limited spatial focusing or may require carefully patterned structures.

Viscoelastic liquids, including polymer-containing aqueous solutions, can exhibit non-Newtonian behavior that modifies particle migration and flow-induced transport. A need exists for a system that uses the combined effects of laminar flow, viscoelastic fluid properties, and an opposing electric field to concentrate suspended molecules or particles at one or more controlled locations.

### Summary  
In one embodiment, an apparatus is provided for concentrating target species suspended in a viscoelastic liquid. The apparatus includes a flow channel configured to support substantially laminar flow of the viscoelastic liquid, an inlet for receiving a sample containing the target species, an outlet for discharging processed liquid, and a pair of electrodes configured to establish an electric field along at least a portion of the flow channel. A pressure source or flow-control element drives the viscoelastic liquid in a first direction, while the electric field produces electrophoretic motion of at least a portion of the target species in a second direction opposite the first direction. Under selected operating conditions, the pressure-driven convective transport and the electric-field-induced transport oppose one another, causing the target species to accumulate in a concentration zone.

In another embodiment, the viscoelastic liquid comprises a carrier liquid and a viscoelastic additive, such as a polymer, biopolymer, surfactant system, or other rheology-modifying agent. The viscoelastic liquid may be selected to provide elastic lift, shear-dependent migration, or enhanced spatial retention of particles within the laminar flow channel.

In another embodiment, a controller regulates flow rate, electric-field strength, fluid composition, temperature, and/or channel geometry to position the concentration zone at a desired location within the channel.

### Brief Description of Numbered System Components  
An exemplary system may include the following numbered components:

1. **Concentration system**  
2. **Microfluidic or mesofluidic channel**  
3. **Channel inlet**  
4. **Channel outlet**  
5. **Sample reservoir**  
6. **Viscoelastic liquid reservoir**  
7. **Pressure source or pump**  
8. **Flow-control valve**  
9. **First electrode**  
10. **Second electrode**  
11. **Electric-field power supply**  
12. **Controller**  
13. **Target molecules or particles**  
14. **Viscoelastic liquid**  
15. **Laminar flow region**  
16. **Concentration zone**  
17. **Detection module**  
18. **Collection port**  
19. **Temperature-control element**  
20. **Data-processing unit**

### Detailed Description  

#### General System Configuration  
Referring to an exemplary embodiment, the concentration system **1** includes a channel **2** having a channel inlet **3** and a channel outlet **4**. The channel **2** may be formed in glass, silicon, polymer, ceramic, metal, or a composite substrate. In some embodiments, the channel **2** is a microchannel having at least one cross-sectional dimension between about 1 micrometer and about 1 millimeter. In other embodiments, the channel **2** is a larger laminar-flow conduit configured to maintain a Reynolds number sufficiently low to avoid turbulent mixing.

The channel inlet **3** is fluidically coupled to a sample reservoir **5** and/or a viscoelastic liquid reservoir **6**. The sample reservoir **5** contains target molecules or particles **13** suspended in, or configured to be mixed with, a viscoelastic liquid **14**. The viscoelastic liquid reservoir **6** may contain a carrier liquid premixed with a polymer or other viscoelastic additive. The channel outlet **4** permits discharge of depleted liquid, concentrated liquid, or waste.

A pressure source or pump **7** is operably connected to the channel **2** to drive the viscoelastic liquid **14** through the channel **2**. The pressure source **7** may include a syringe pump, pressure regulator, peristaltic pump, electrokinetic pump, capillary-pressure source, or gravity-feed device. A flow-control valve **8** may be provided to regulate flow rate, stop flow, pulse flow, or direct liquid to selected downstream pathways.

A first electrode **9** and a second electrode **10** are disposed to generate an electric field within at least a portion of the channel **2**. The electrodes **9**, **10** may be positioned in reservoirs, embedded in the channel wall, arranged along the channel length, or connected through conductive gels, salt bridges, or electrode chambers. An electric-field power supply **11** applies a voltage or current between the first electrode **9** and the second electrode **10**. The field may be direct current, pulsed direct current, alternating current with a nonzero effective bias, or a programmed waveform.

A controller **12** may be coupled to the pressure source **7**, the valve **8**, and the power supply **11**. The controller **12** regulates operating parameters so that the bulk laminar flow transports the viscoelastic liquid **14** in a first axial direction while the electric field causes electrophoretic migration of charged target molecules or particles **13** in a second axial direction opposite the first direction.

#### Viscoelastic Liquid  
The viscoelastic liquid **14** may comprise water, buffer, saline, organic solvent, ionic liquid, hydrogel precursor, oil, or a mixture thereof, together with a viscoelastic additive. Suitable additives include, but are not limited to, polyethylene oxide, polyacrylamide, polyvinylpyrrolidone, hyaluronic acid, xanthan gum, DNA, methylcellulose, carboxymethyl cellulose, wormlike micelles, surfactant systems, or combinations thereof.

The viscoelastic liquid **14** may have a relaxation time sufficient to produce elastic stresses under flow through the channel **2**. In some embodiments, the Deborah number or Weissenberg number is selected such that elastic forces influence particle migration, streamline retention, or dispersion. The viscosity, elasticity, ionic strength, pH, and conductivity of the viscoelastic liquid **14** may be selected according to the charge, size, diffusivity, and stability of the target species **13**.

#### Target Species  
The target molecules or particles **13** may include charged molecules, nucleic acids, proteins, peptides, polysaccharides, extracellular vesicles, viruses, bacteria, cells, organelles, beads, droplets, colloids, nanoparticles, microparticles, or aggregates thereof. The target species **13** may have an electrophoretic mobility of sufficient magnitude and polarity such that, upon application of the electric field, the species experiences motion opposed to the bulk flow direction.

In certain embodiments, the target species **13** may be labeled with a charged tag or affinity reagent to adjust electrophoretic mobility. In other embodiments, the pH or ionic composition of the viscoelastic liquid **14** is selected to provide the target species **13** with a desired net charge.

#### Laminar Flow and Opposing Electric Field  
During operation, the pressure source **7** drives the viscoelastic liquid **14** through the channel **2**, producing a laminar flow region **15**. The Reynolds number may be maintained below a threshold, for example below about 2000, below about 100, below about 10, or below about 1, depending on the channel dimensions and application.

The electric-field power supply **11** applies a potential difference between the first electrode **9** and the second electrode **10** to create an electric field along the channel **2**. The field is oriented such that electrophoretic motion of the target species **13** is at least partially opposite to the pressure-driven flow. When the convective velocity of the bulk liquid and the electrophoretic velocity of the target species **13** are balanced at a particular axial location, the target species **13** may accumulate, forming a concentration zone **16**.

The concentration zone **16** may be stationary, quasi-stationary, or slowly translatable along the channel **2**. The location of the concentration zone **16** may depend on one or more of flow velocity, electric-field strength, channel cross-section, surface charge, viscoelastic properties, particle size, electrophoretic mobility, and local ionic conductivity.

In some embodiments, the viscoelastic nature of the liquid **14** suppresses axial dispersion or promotes cross-stream migration of particles into regions of reduced or increased flow velocity. This may enhance accumulation by increasing the residence time of particles near the balance point between pressure-driven and electrophoretic transport.

#### Detection and Collection  
A detection module **17** may be positioned adjacent to the concentration zone **16**. The detection module **17** may include an optical detector, fluorescence detector, absorbance detector, Raman detector, impedance sensor, electrochemical sensor, camera, photodiode, or microscope objective. The detection module **17** may monitor formation, intensity, size, or position of the concentration zone **16**.

A collection port **18** may be fluidically coupled to the channel **2** at or near the concentration zone **16**. After concentration, the controller **12** may reduce the electric field, increase flow rate, actuate the valve **8**, or otherwise direct the enriched target species **13** into the collection port **18**. Alternatively, concentrated species may be analyzed in situ without collection.

A temperature-control element **19** may be provided to maintain fluid temperature, reduce Joule heating, stabilize viscosity, or protect biological samples. The temperature-control element **19** may include a Peltier device, heat sink, circulating fluid jacket, resistive heater, temperature sensor, or feedback control loop.

A data-processing unit **20** may receive signals from the detection module **17** and adjust operating parameters through the controller **12**. For example, the data-processing unit **20** may implement feedback control to maintain the concentration zone **16** at a fixed location by adjusting the voltage applied by the power supply **11** or the flow rate provided by the pump **7**.

### Exemplary Operation  
In one exemplary method, a sample containing target particles **13** is introduced from the sample reservoir **5** into the channel **2** together with the viscoelastic liquid **14**. The pressure source **7** establishes laminar flow in a downstream direction from the inlet **3** toward the outlet **4**. The power supply **11** applies an electric field between the electrodes **9**, **10** such that the electrophoretic velocity of the target particles **13** is upstream relative to the bulk flow.

The flow rate and electric-field strength are adjusted until a concentration zone **16** forms within the laminar flow region **15**. Particles entering the region from upstream are slowed or retained by the opposing electric field, while particles diffusing or migrating upstream are returned toward the concentration zone by the imposed hydrodynamic flow. As a result, the particles accumulate in a localized region.

After a desired concentration factor is achieved, the concentrated particles may be detected by the detection module **17**, collected through the collection port **18**, or transported to a downstream assay chamber by changing the flow or field conditions.

### Optional Variations  
In some embodiments, the channel **2** includes a constriction, expansion, curved segment, serpentine portion, or tapered region to modify local flow velocity and elastic stresses. The concentration zone **16** may be positioned near such a geometric feature.

In some embodiments, multiple electrode pairs are arranged along the channel **2** to form multiple concentration zones or to move a concentrated plug in a stepwise manner. In other embodiments, the electric field is time-modulated to alternately concentrate and release the target species **13**.

In some embodiments, the channel **2** includes a surface coating to reduce adsorption, control electroosmotic flow, or improve compatibility with biological samples. Suitable coatings include hydrophilic polymers, zwitterionic coatings, silanes, proteins, hydrogels, or polyelectrolyte multilayers.

In some embodiments, the system **1** is integrated into a lab-on-a-chip device including sample preparation, reagent mixing, washing, labeling, detection, and waste handling. In other embodiments, the system **1** is configured as a continuous-flow concentrator for preparative enrichment of particles or molecules.

### Advantages  
The disclosed system may provide one or more advantages, including concentration without a physical membrane, reduced clogging, compatibility with fragile biological species, tunable concentration location, continuous-flow operation, low sample-volume requirements, and integration with optical or electrical detection. The use of a viscoelastic liquid may improve retention, focusing, or enrichment relative to purely Newtonian systems under comparable laminar-flow and electric-field conditions.

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a formal invention summary for a microfluidic concentration device using viscoelastic liquid, where an intake cross-section is larger than each outlet channel and a modulation unit reduces the electric field after concentration.
counterfactuals.output:
A microfluidic concentration device is disclosed for concentrating particles, biomolecules, cells, or other target substances in a viscoelastic liquid medium. The device includes a microfluidic channel structure having an intake channel, a concentration region, and a plurality of outlet channels. The intake channel is configured with a cross-sectional area greater than the cross-sectional area of each individual outlet channel, thereby facilitating controlled introduction of a sample-containing viscoelastic liquid and promoting hydrodynamic and viscoelastic focusing of target constituents within the concentration region.

The viscoelastic liquid generates elastic lift forces and flow-induced migration effects that act on suspended target materials as the liquid passes through the microfluidic structure. Under an applied electric field, the target materials are transported and concentrated in a predetermined region of the device. The relative dimensional configuration between the larger intake cross-section and the smaller outlet channels enhances concentration efficiency by increasing residence time, improving focusing behavior, and enabling selective discharge through one or more outlet channels.

The device further includes an electric-field modulation unit operatively coupled to electrodes or field-generating elements associated with the microfluidic channel. The modulation unit is configured to reduce the electric field after a concentration event or after a desired concentration level has been reached. By lowering the electric field following concentration, the device reduces undesirable effects such as Joule heating, electrolysis, particle damage, sample dispersion, and excessive electrokinetic transport. The modulation unit may operate automatically in response to a detected concentration threshold, elapsed time, flow condition, impedance change, optical signal, or other feedback parameter.

In one embodiment, the microfluidic concentration device comprises a substrate defining the intake channel, concentration region, and outlet channels; a viscoelastic liquid flowing through the substrate-defined microchannels; an electrode arrangement for applying an electric field across at least a portion of the concentration region; and a controller configured to modulate the applied electric field by decreasing the field strength after concentration. The outlet channels may be arranged downstream of the concentration region to separate concentrated and non-concentrated fractions, with each outlet channel having a smaller cross-section than the intake channel.

The invention provides a compact and efficient platform for concentrating analytes in microfluidic systems while improving post-concentration stability and reducing adverse electrical effects. The device is suitable for use in biological analysis, diagnostics, sample preparation, cell sorting, nanoparticle concentration, and lab-on-a-chip applications.
